<div id="main" class="col-md-9" role="main">

# matchdb

<div class="section level1">

A disambiguation database for nonprofit record linkage: every name and
address the IRS and 990 filers have recorded for each EIN, with its
source, normalized once and compiled on demand into the reference frame
that
[npmatch](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/npmatch)
matches against.

It is **not** a matching engine. Blocking, comparison, vetoes, scoring
and tiering live in npmatch.

<div class="section level2">

## Install

<div id="cb1" class="sourceCode">

``` r
remotes::install_github("Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/matchdb@v0.1.1")  # the current release
remotes::install_github("Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/matchdb")         # development version
```

</div>

The current release is **0.1.1**, git tag `v0.1.1`. It pairs with
npmatch 0.1.1 and normalizer signature `v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e`. Pin it, in
renv or with `@v0.1.1`, for anything that should reproduce results from
before the normalizer moved into npnormalize.

**The published data moved on 2026-11-01.** The database, bundles and
tranches online are now built with npnormalize 0.1.3, signature
`v1-592912060053c4c3`. Only the development version reads them; 0.1.1
refuses them, as the signature check intends. See
[NEWS.md](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/NEWS.md).

The development version takes the normalizer from
[npnormalize](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/npnormalize)
and only suggests npmatch. Three packages are involved, and both sides
of a match have to use the same normalizer:

| package     | role                                                                                          | install for the published data                                         |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| npnormalize | turns names and addresses into keys; its signature is stamped on everything matchdb publishes | **0.1.3**, the commit below                                            |
| matchdb     | the database and the references                                                               | the development version                                                |
| npmatch     | matches your records against a reference                                                      | the development version; 0.1.1 still carries its own, older normalizer |

<div id="cb2" class="sourceCode">

``` r
remotes::install_github("Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/npnormalize@6d9c669")  # 0.1.3
remotes::install_github("Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/npmatch", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/matchdb", upgrade = "never")
```

</div>

`upgrade = "never"` keeps npnormalize at 0.1.3. **npnormalize 0.1.4
moves the signature again**, to `v1-1179714ce1e9d31f`, and the data
published on 2026-11-01 is refused under it until it is rebuilt. Check
what you have with `npnormalize::np_normalize_signature()`.

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Quick start: download a reference and match

[Getting
started](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/matchdb.html)
walks through a full example: matching four grant recipients, reading
the results, and looking at the cases that are not clear-cut.

Four references are published, built from the database. Downloading one
needs no AWS account.

| label              | EINs              | names                                    |  rows |
|--------------------|-------------------|------------------------------------------|------:|
| `active-legal`     | current BMF       | legal, DBA                               | 2.74M |
| `active-observed`  | current BMF       | legal, DBA, aliases written by 2+ filers | 2.88M |
| `unified-legal`    | every BMF release | legal, DBA                               | 4.98M |
| `unified-observed` | every BMF release | legal, DBA, aliases written by 2+ filers | 5.13M |

<div id="cb3" class="sourceCode">

``` r
library(matchdb)
b <- md_reference("active-observed", fetch = "missing")   # ~290 MB, once

m <- npmatch::np_cascade(my_query, b$reference,
                         name_freq = b$name_freq, token_idf = b$token_idf,
                         ref_index = b$ref_index)
```

</div>

Each bundle is checked against the md5s it was published with and
against the installed normalizer (npnormalize’s signature). A stale or
altered bundle is refused.

A bundle also carries `b$addr_freq` (how crowded each address is),
`b$places` and `b$clusters` (the families its organizations belong to),
which npmatch’s `np_pair_links()` and `np_cluster_rollup()` read.

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Look up an organization

With the database downloaded (`md_fetch_db()`, 11.8 GB):

<div id="cb4" class="sourceCode">

``` r
md_lookup("53-0196605")    # entity, names, addresses, events, relations, clusters, ...
md_cluster("53-0196605")   # its families: group ruling, Schedule R system, shared site, ...
```

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Compile your own slice

A reference is described by a spec with these settings:

-   **layers**: which EINs.
-   **name and address classes**: which strings.
-   **sources**: who reported them.
-   **corroboration**: how many filers must agree on an alias.

<div id="cb5" class="sourceCode">

``` r
s <- md_spec(layers = c("bmf_active", "bmf_inactive"),
             names = c("legal", "dba", "observed"),
             addresses = c("mailing", "observed"),
             min_corroborators = 2)
r <- md_compile(s)         # r$reference, r$name_freq, r$token_idf, r$report
```

</div>

You don’t need the whole database for this. The database is also
published as parquet files split by layer and class, and
`md_fetch_tranches()` downloads only the files a spec needs:

<div id="cb6" class="sourceCode">

``` r
md_fetch_tranches(s)       # only these layers and classes, once
con <- md_tranche_db()     # a connection md_compile(), md_publish() and md_lookup() take
r <- md_compile(s, con)
md_db_close(con)
```

</div>

`md_tranches(s)` shows what a spec will download before you fetch it.
Every fetch, compile and publish is logged in your matchdb folder:
`md_log()` lists them, and `md_status()` says what is there now.
`md_tranche_diff()` shows what a new release changes. See
`vignette("workspace")`.

The articles explain each choice:

| article                                                                                               | question                                                    |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| [Layers](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/layers.html)               | which organizations a reference can match                   |
| [Sources](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/sources.html)             | where each name and address comes from                      |
| [Corroborators](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/corroborators.html) | how much to trust a name someone else wrote                 |
| [Families](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/clusters.html)           | which EINs belong together when no single one can be chosen |

Two more explain how the database works: [how corroboration is counted
and
recorded](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/corroboration-ledger.html),
and [how the database is
updated](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/matchdb/articles/updates.html).

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## What is in the database

Built from pinned versions of the IRS Business Master File, 990 e-file
headers, Schedules I, R and C, Form 1023-EZ approvals, the 990-N
e-Postcard, the automatic-revocation list, Part VII officer name keys,
and NCCS address history and geocodes. That gives 4.24M EINs, 12.8M name
rows and 22.0M address rows. Relations between EINs and typed clusters
are built on top.

Every name and address is a rollup of an append-only observation ledger
(48.3M observations), which records which release of which source said
it, and, for a third party, which filer. The ledger ships only in the
maintainer copy, `MATCHDB-full.duckdb` (24.2 GB). `dev/build-matchdb.R`
rebuilds the database from scratch in about 70 minutes. `dev/PLAN.md` is
the design, and `dev/PROCESS.md` records the verification gates.

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Related repositories

| repo                                                                         | role                                                                                                                                     |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [npnormalize](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/npnormalize) | the normalizer and its signature. matchdb imports it, and so does npmatch, so both sides of a match key names and addresses the same way |
| [npmatch](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/npmatch)         | the record-linkage engine. matchdb only suggests it; it reads matchdb’s references and depends on nothing here                           |
| [pfmatch](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/pfmatch)         | 990-PF grant-recipient matching: the first consumer, and the benchmark                                                                   |
| [ef2](https://github.com/Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/ef2)                 | IRS 990 e-file processing                                                                                                                |

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div id="main" class="col-md-9" role="main">

# Package index

<div class="section level2">

## Get a reference and match

<div class="section-desc">

Download a published reference, or the whole database, and read it in
the form npmatch matches against.

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_publish()` `md_publish_pointer()` `md_reference()` : Publish a
    compiled reference, and read one back
-   `md_fetch_reference()` `md_fetch_db()` `md_remote()` : Download
    published references, or the whole database

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Your matchdb folder

<div class="section-desc">

What is published and what is here, the log of everything fetched,
compiled and published, and updating to a new build.

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_tranches()` `md_tranche_manifest()` `md_tranche_diff()`
    `md_tranches_prune()` : What tranches are published, what they cost,
    and what changed
-   `md_log()` `md_log_run()` `md_status()` : The workspace log: what
    was fetched, compiled and published, and when

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Look things up

<div class="section-desc">

Everything the database knows about an EIN, and the families it belongs
to.

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_lookup()` `md_lookup_parts()` : Everything the database knows
    about an EIN
-   `md_cluster()` : The families an EIN belongs to, and who else is in
    them
-   `md_ein()` `md_is_ein()` : The canonical EIN format

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Compile and publish your own slice

<div class="section-desc">

Describe a reference by layer, name and address class, source and
corroboration; compile it; publish it as a stamped bundle.

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_spec()` : Describe a reference: which EINs, which names, which
    addresses

-   `md_compile()` : Compile a spec into the reference frame npmatch
    matches against

-   `md_publish()` `md_publish_pointer()` `md_reference()` : Publish a
    compiled reference, and read one back

-   `md_publish_tranches()` `md_tranche_pointer()` `md_fetch_tranches()`
    `md_tranche_db()` : Publish the database as parquet tranches, fetch
    only what a spec needs

-   `md_relations()` `md_layers()` `md_name_classes()`
    `md_address_classes()` : The frozen enumerations, as code

-   `md_name_sources()` `md_address_sources()` :

    Source-bit registries for `source_mask`

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## The database

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_db()` `md_db_close()` : Open the matchdb database
-   `md_data_root()` `md_path()` `md_data_init()` : Where matchdb keeps
    its data

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Sources and provenance

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_sources()` : The source registry
-   `md_source_urls()` : URLs for a year-partitioned source
-   `md_source_head()` : Read upstream object metadata without
    downloading it
-   `md_source_pin()` `md_source_read_pin()` `md_source_read_files()` :
    Pin a source to a concrete, immutable version
-   `md_source_moved()` : Has an upstream pointer moved since we pinned
    it?
-   `md_source_kinds()` : The kinds of source
-   `md_record_vintage()` : Record an ingest in the audit table
-   `md_relations()` `md_layers()` `md_name_classes()`
    `md_address_classes()` : The frozen enumerations, as code
-   `md_f1023ez_urls` : The 1023-EZ approval URLs are not consistently
    named
-   `md_meta_caveats` : Known hazards in the NCCS metadata name and
    address files

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Stable ids

<div class="section-desc">

Content-hash ids for names, addresses, observations and releases, the
same in R and in SQL (dev/IDENTITY.md).

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_canon()` `md_hash_id()` `md_name_text_id()`
    `md_address_text_id()` `md_release_id()` : Canonical text and
    content-hash ids
-   `md_id_recipes()` : The id recipes
-   `md_identity_macros()` : Install the id macros in a DuckDB
    connection
-   `md_record_keys()` : The natural key of each source
-   `md_check_record_key()` : Check a source's natural key on a loaded
    file
-   `md_text_schema()` `md_add_text()` `md_build_text()`
    `md_build_text_derived()` `md_check_text_derived()`
    `md_text_stats()` : Text dictionaries and derived columns keyed on
    the text
-   `md_ledger_schema()` : The observation ledger
-   `md_apply_release()` : Fold one release of a source into the ledger
-   `md_parse_efile_header()` `md_parse_schedi()`
    `md_parse_bmf_active()` `md_parse_address_crosswalk()`
    `md_parse_bmf_unified()` `md_parse_f1023ez()`
    `md_parse_efile_related()` `md_parse_affiliate_listing()`
    `md_parse_e_postcard()` `md_parse_revocations()` : Parse a raw
    source file into a ledger frame
-   `md_build_ledger()` : Load the pinned source files into the ledger
-   `md_build_rollups()` `md_compare_rollups()` `md_install_rollups()` :
    Build name and address from the ledger
-   `md_link_derived()` : Rebuild name_derived and address_derived from
    the text-keyed columns
-   `md_normalizer_diff()` : What a new normalizer would change

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Building the database

<div class="section-desc">

The ingests, in the order dev/build-matchdb.R runs them, then the
derived tables. Most users never call these.

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_ingest_address_crosswalk()` : Ingest the resolved address
    crosswalk as historical spells

-   `md_ingest_affiliate_listing()` : Add group-return rosters: the
    subordinate names the BMF throws away

-   `md_ingest_bmf()` `md_validate_bmf()` : Ingest the unified BMF into
    entity, name and address

-   `md_ingest_efile_group()` : Add group membership from what filers
    report on Form 990 line H

-   `md_ingest_efile_header()` : Ingest the 990 filing header as
    self-reported names and addresses

-   `md_ingest_e_postcard()` : Ingest the Form 990-N e-Postcard

-   `md_ingest_f1023ez()` : Ingest Form 1023-EZ approvals

-   `md_ingest_geocode()` : Attach census geography to the addresses it
    actually describes

-   `md_ingest_group_meta()` : Add historical group membership from the
    NCCS group metadata

-   `md_ingest_irs527_related()` : Add related entities disclosed on 527
    Schedule R

-   `md_ingest_ntee()` : Fill the resolved NTEE triple on entity

-   `md_ingest_officers()` : Ingest officer, director and key-employee
    name keys from Form 990 Part VII

-   `md_ingest_orgtext()` : Ingest mission and program text

-   `md_ingest_relations()` : Build ein_relation from Schedule R and the
    group exemption structure

-   `md_ingest_revocations()` : Ingest the IRS automatic revocation list

-   `md_ingest_schedi()` : Ingest Schedule I recipient aliases as
    observed names and addresses

-   `md_ingest_schedr()` : Ingest Schedule R related organisations as
    observed names and addresses

-   `md_ingest_schedr_parts()` : Add the other three identification
    parts of Schedule R

-   `md_ingest_sched_c_affil()` : Add the Schedule C affiliated-group
    roster

-   `md_ingest_websites()` : Ingest organisation websites

-   `md_build_derived()` : Build the derived-column tables

-   `md_check_derived_fresh()` : Has a re-ingest invalidated the derived
    tables?

-   `md_build_compact()` : Build the compact identity tables

-   `md_build_groups()` :

    Build `group_id`: the federated families in `ein_relation`

-   `md_build_places()` : Places: how crowded an address is, and what
    kind of place it is

-   `md_place_key()` `md_unit_id()` : npnormalize's address key and
    suite identifier

-   `md_addr_freq()` : Address-sharing statistics for a compiled
    reference

-   `md_build_ein_key()` :

    Build `ein_key`: every identifier an EIN holds, with how specific it
    is

-   `md_build_clusters()` : Build the cluster layer: typed, many-to-many
    families of EINs

-   `md_build_stats()` : Build the per-cell corpus statistics

-   `md_ntee_canonical` : The NTEE crosswalk is canonical, and its
    nteev2 columns are not

-   `md_irs527_shape` : What the 527 files can and cannot support

-   `md_schedb_excluded` : Why 527 Schedule B is not a matchdb source

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Checks and guards

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_validate()` `md_validate_report()` : Intrinsic validation of a
    built table
-   `md_ingest_bmf()` `md_validate_bmf()` : Ingest the unified BMF into
    entity, name and address
-   `md_ntee_crosscheck()` : Compare the 1023-EZ NTEE against the
    resolved value
-   `md_guard_observed()` : Guards on observed names: is the written
    name really this EIN's?
-   `md_guard_key()` : Name key used by the guards
-   `md_placeholder_ein()` : Placeholder EINs
-   `md_name_pair_hit()` : Do two name keys name the same organisation
    by an abbreviation rule?

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Verification harness

<div class="section-desc">

Comparing references and match results between builds (the phase gates).

</div>

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_normal_form()` : Put a frame in comparison normal form
-   `md_compare_frames()` : Compare two frames against the gate
    criterion
-   `md_compare_tiered()` : Compare two tiered benchmark outputs

</div>

<div class="section level2">

## Utilities

</div>

<div class="section level2">

-   `md_modal_sql()` : Deterministically pick a representative value
-   `md_light_key()` : The light key ingests group spellings on
-   `md_xlsx_to_csv()` : Extract named columns from a large .xlsx by
    streaming its XML

</div>

</div>
